description.p: Rookparcel is a lean BitTorrent client in the spirit of µTorrent 2.2.1: small, fast, native and comfortable with thousands of torrents. Its engine is a Rust port of libtorrent-rasterbar.

ul.li: Downloads and seeds over TCP and uTP, with HTTP, HTTPS and UDP trackers
Magnet links, DHT, peer exchange and local peer discovery
Encryption, web seeds, proxies, UPnP and NAT-PMP, IP filters
A tray icon, desktop notifications and Auto Shutdown

description.p: Rookparcel is pre-alpha: settings and saved state may change between versions. It is source-available under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0, so it is free for noncommercial use only.
The AppImages are built on Ubuntu 22.04, so they run on Ubuntu 22.04 and Debian 12 too. Nothing else changes.
The desktop entry declares version 1.0 of the desktop entry specification, so older validators, such as the AppImage catalog's, accept it. Nothing else changes.

A new Gaming page in Preferences, just above Advanced, gathers what keeps games, calls and the computer responsive: Keep ping low (from Bandwidth) and the smart disk I/O settings (from Advanced > Disk I/O). Checking torrents gently is now off unless you turn it on there.

Adding many torrents is fast again: since 1.2.57 every added torrent waited for the settings file to be written to the disk, even when the settings had not changed. They are now written only when they change, as safe against a crash as before.

A torrent whose drive or share is gone keeps its pieces: it stops with "files missing" and starts again by itself when the storage is back, instead of downloading everything again. Force Re-Check starts a stopped torrent. A check waiting for its drive says "Queued for checking", and the release carries the fixes of a full review of the code.
The Trackers and Peers tabs sort by their columns: click a header to sort, again to reverse, a third time for the original order. Selected peers stay selected as the list updates.
The Files tab sorts by its columns: click a header to sort, again to reverse, a third time for the torrent's own order. Selected files stay selected as their rows move.

A finished torrent in which you tick another file now looks for peers at once: it asks its trackers, the DHT and local peer discovery again and reconnects to the seeds it had let go, instead of showing Downloading without peers for a minute or more.

Tags, as in qBittorrent. Sequential download and first and last pieces first for previewing a video. Unfinished files can carry .!ut until complete, and partial files from µTorrent and qBittorrent are picked up. Files can be left out by name, and the IP filter's block list can come from an https address. The window lock has its own page under Preferences > Advanced.

Settings are checked after every update: if a new version reads the proxy or the network binding differently from the one that saved them, the transfers are held until you confirm the settings, and a copy of the old settings file is kept. A settings file that cannot be read is never overwritten.

Lock Rookparcel: a PIN of 4 to 6 digits hides its windows in the tray until the PIN is typed, also across restarts; --reset-lock removes a forgotten PIN. Web seeds work for a v2-only torrent with one file. A second stop signal no longer ends the app while it saves.
A file that is gone no longer makes a start hash the whole torrent: only that file is downloaded again. The Logger leaves out the "received N peers" lines.

Seeds are no longer stopped at a ratio of 1.5 by default: the seeding goal acts only once it is switched on in Preferences > Queueing. A torrent started again after its goal keeps seeding. The Logger says which goal stopped a torrent.

Help > Statistics with all-time totals. Trackers added to new downloads, typed or from a list on the web. Run Program when a torrent is added or finishes. Closing while a torrent waits for its check no longer makes the next start hash every file. The Logger leaves out trackers that do not answer. Help > Donate. Lower buttons and fields.

Less CPU use while idle: the app no longer reads every torrent's metadata again after each start when its Web UI is on, and local peer discovery no longer looks at every stopped torrent several times a second.
Dark mode on Windows (following the system, or chosen), nine themes and your own CSS themes for the Web UI, and dark-theme fixes for the GTK app's drawn parts, icons and scheduler.

The Files tab shows the torrent's files in their folders, as the Add Torrent dialog does; a Tree view button gives back the single list of paths. The Add Torrent dialog gets a file filter and type-ahead. The app no longer closes on some systems as soon as a torrent is listed.

A magnet stopped from its Add dialog now reconnects to its peer at once when it is started, instead of a minute later. The rest of this release is the new native macOS app; the Linux GUI is otherwise unchanged.

PaTorrent is now Rookparcel, with a new icon, the Postal Rook. Settings, torrents, profiles and portable folders from PaTorrent are taken over at the first start. A Web UI login refused after a ban is now answered as banned.

Profiles run several independent Rookparcels side by side, and portable mode keeps one in a folder that can move between drives and systems. A Setup Guide at the first start, help for every setting, a filter in the Files tab, binding torrent traffic to a VPN, and an optional search helper that fetches Jackett for you are new. A bug hunt fixed 37 problems, among them a Web UI login bypass and a peer message that crashed the engine.

A gamer mode keeps your ping low by slowing transfers down when your line starts to queue. Smart disk I/O checks torrents gently, one per drive, tells SSDs, hard disks and network shares apart, and can slow down while a disk is busy. A window shows what Rookparcel is doing while it closes, the Files tab has µTorrent 2.2.1's menu, completed downloads can move into a folder named after their label, and the engine carries the applicable fixes from libtorrent 2.0.12 to 2.1.2.

Torrent search through your own Prowlarr or Jackett, the RSS Downloader in the Windows client's Web UI, an optional API key and subnet whitelist for Sonarr, Radarr and Prowlarr, and an update check in the headless daemon.

Sonarr, Radarr and Prowlarr work with Rookparcel as their download client: seed limits arrive with each grab and Remove Completed removes finished torrents. Idle seeds keep counting their seeding time, adding a torrent brings the window forward, and a torrent added stopped reads Stopped.

The Windows GUI serves its own Web UI from Preferences, so a browser shows and drives that window's torrents. The daemon's Windows service command stores the Web UI login hashed and can replace and start an installed service in one step.

A search box that filters the torrent list by name, importing torrents from qBittorrent and µTorrent, security hardening across the engine, the Web UI and the remote mode, and icons beside the category list, the detail tabs and the Preferences pages.
First stable release. The window title and the tray tooltip show the version.
First public release candidate for 1.0.
First pre-alpha build of the GTK GUI as a Flatpak.
